items.title: Sudhalter interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2019
items.q: I would guess that David Berger’s situation tonight might be the same... I think he teaches at a major Manhattan school or something.

ctx.x: And I often wonder well how does that work? How do you play all those people? Do they mostly do it, like it’s an off night and —

You know I mean especially if you know I think the most offers that come in for big band are to play the old nostalgic kind of repertoire. And to pay people $10 to do that it’s really insulting. I mean I guess that David Berger — probably people are going because the arrangements are worth playing. Almost any jazz musician will do a rehearsal band. We have lots of rehearsal bands in New York City. If you go up to the union on 48th Street, any time of any day, just walk in and you’ll hear some band rehearsing with…

good arrangements and I would guess that David Berger’s situation tonight might be the same, or maybe he is paying well with a grant, I don’t know. But probably not. The opportunity to play at Birdland, and then the opportunity to play something that’s really quality — or maybe he has his students playing. Who knows? I think he teaches at a major Manhattan school or something. Juilliard or something.
